newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia cenbank details new portfolio regulations.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia cenbank details new portfolio regulations.

text.p: The Slovenian central bank said on Thursday its decision to force foreign investors to trade through special custody or fiduciary accounts at fully licenced banks was a step towards regulating the stock market.
"This is not a freeze of foreign portfolio investment, it simply regulates it," Janko Tratnik, head of the foreign business department at the Bank of Slovenia, told Reuters.
From Monday, foreign investors can only buy Slovenian shares through new accounts at a Slovenian bank. Previously, they did not need to hold an account in order to buy shares.
"The new regulation was not introduced in order to discourage foreign investors but aims to increase transparency and is in line with regulations abroad," the Bank of Slovenia said earlier.

The central bank said there were no limits regarding inflow or outflow on new accounts, except when cash transactions were concerned. Cash withdrawals are limited to 250,000 tolars ($1,655) per month.

Out of 28 Slovenian banks, 14 have a full licence. Four of those are in partial foreign ownership -- SKB bank, Bank Austria, Creditanstalt and Volksbank-Ljudska banka. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
